chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Players back East studying him; fast tenor and Chico Hamilton
summary: Coltrane and others checked him out, he was among the first to play fast tenor, and Chico Hamilton remembered him.

bands.name: Joe Liggins and His Honey Drippers

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: But you later found out that John Coltrane was hearing your records.
Oh yeah. All the guys back East, the saxophone players, they were back there checking me out, and I'm out here -- I don't know what's going on, you know.
I've read some people say that you were playing things that Coltrane was later given credit for; you were doing them first.

Well, a whole lot of guys... Actually, I was one of the first guys really playing fast on the tenor saxophone. In a liner note Leonard Feather did some time ago for an album that Sonny Rollins didn't finish out, and they had some tracks they had gotten from Joe Castro up at his house, up at Falcon's Lair, when he was living at Doris Duke's case, at the old Rudolph Valentino home, and we had done some things... Just recording things in there. But Leonard had heard them, so he bought the rest of the tracks
that he needed to fill out this album.

And in the liner notes, he mentioned the fact that Chico Hamilton, the drummer, had mentioned on an interview that they had together on the radio in Chicago some time back that there was a guy out in California who was playing the way the guys are playing now a long time ago. In fact, the only thing he had heard really change a lot was the saxophone players, you know. And he was talking about I had been playing this type of horn that became popular later on a long time ago. He heard me playing it out here.

Because he was from here. This was his home. In fact, right after I first came out, he was in the Navy, and they had a band together down at the Downbeat Club with John Anderson and Buddy Collette and Red Callender, and I think Gerry Wiggins might have been with that band, the great... yeah, I think he might have been with that band -- and Britt Woodman on trombone. And later on, I heard the Honey Dripper band, Joe Liggins and His Honey Drippers. They became real popular, and they used to work the Downbeat Club quite a bit.
